newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Independent TV filming barred at Russia parliament.
newsitem.headline: Independent TV filming barred at Russia parliament.

text.p: The communist-dominated State Duma lower house of the Russian parliament voted on Wednesday to bar independent television filming of its debates, prompting President Boris Yeltsin's representative to complain of censorship.
The Duma approved by 264-30 a resolution that gave its press service a monopoly right to film debates.
The new rules allow television companies, both Russian and foreign, to use the official footage, but each of them has to work out conditions under which it will receive the material.
Duma deputies accused leading television programmes of giving unbalanced accounts of debates.

"Journalists will receive controlled information, set by some unconstitutional, illegal group, and that is censorship," Yeltsin's representative in the Duma, Aleksander Kotenkov, told RIA news agency.
Until now television companies were allowed to film Russian parliamentary debates.

"This decision can be explained by one of two reasons, either they want to show us how to work, or not to show us what is happening in the parliament," the evening news anchor on Russian public television said.
